full_results: kept with the work, not in this package (the full file exceeds the package file limit)
subject: worst-case Ir of the unbatched rare-path primitives of the secp256k1 rho kernel (step.c)
compile_flags: cc -O3 -fno-tree-vectorize -mgeneral-regs-only (plus -g, which does not change the generated code, verified by comparing disassembly; plus -DNO_LEAVES for the primitive builds and -DBRANCHY for the branchy build)

units: ir_per_call is Ir per call of the noinline wrapper of the primitive as measured: it includes the measuring loop and the call (5 to 7 Ir, listed as harness_loop_ir per primitive). ir_per_call_net_of_harness_loop subtracts them. ir_per_call = (Ir(2N) - Ir(N)) / N, which equals floor(summary Ir / N) because the fixed Callgrind offset is below N; ir_over_n is summary / N.

esc_repeat_max.note: ring check of an escape target (esc_repeat): miss with a full ring runs four comparisons then stores

canon_k_exact_comparison_depth_feasibili.claim: The static bound exceeds the measured maximum only through canon_k_exact paths in which both four-limb comparison chains run to the last limb. For x != 0 the depth pair (d1, d2) needs a nonzero lattice point (d, e), e = c*d mod p, c = beta+1 or beta, with |d| < 2^(64(5-d1)) and |e| < 2^(64(5-d2)); the table shows there is none for (4,4), (4,3), (3,4) and that the boxes (4,2), (3,3), (2,4) hold a few points whose realized depths sum to at most 5. Equal chains happen only for x = 0 (beta x = x or beta^2 x = x forces x = 0). So the worst canon_k_exact path is x = 0 (all eight limbs equal, 182 Ir in the function), and the largest mismatch path is depth (4,1) at 179 Ir.

x_selectors.description: x values for the canon_k variants: r0/r1/r2 random with exact k = 0/1/2 on the fast path; zero (x = 0, fallback, k = 0); latp/latn/lat2p/lat2n and h1..h12 from the lattice of x with beta*x or beta^2*x close to x; nearp (x = p-1, a3 above the fast-path limit, fallback); fb1/fb2 found by search with the fast path rejecting them

composed_from_maxima.rare_2cycle_formula: f_single_max + same_class_max + escape_max_2 + select_adder_max + is_dp_macro_max + esc_repeat_max + 43 (own lines), all net of harness loops

composed_from_maxima.note: Derived by summation; every primitive taken at its own maximum, which the primitives can all attain together except as noted. Not itself measured. Compare with the whole-function static bounds of the unmodified step.c above.

finv_inclusive_ir_per_call.note: finv has no data-dependent branch (its 7 conditional branches are loop counters), so these are exact. The harness copy is 36 Ir more expensive than the one in the unmodified step.c (different inlining of sf_sqr); anything that calls finv is therefore conservative by about that much in the harness.

static_longest_path_unmodified_step_c_ir.method: longest path over all control-flow paths of the function in the binary built from the unmodified step.c with the organizer flags (every conditional branch free, abort paths excluded, finv at its measured cost). In this binary f_single, escape, canon_point, same_class, point_is_dp, select_adder and key_full are inlined into rare_2cycle / rare_anchor, so these two numbers include all of the rare functions' own code. rare_anchor: the while-loop header is visited at most 65 times (len 1..64 plus the failing test) and the escape loop header at most 64 times (len <= 65). The bounds contain paths that cannot occur together (for example canon_k_exact comparison chains at full depth in every call), so they are upper bounds, not attained values.

ii_per_call_stable_when_N_doubles.method: every variant was run at N and at 2N (N=1000 for most; 300 for escape len 65; 400/100/20 for the rare_anchor scenarios); ir_per_call = (Ir(2N) - Ir(N)) / N is an exact integer for every variant, and Ir(N) = N * ir_per_call + a fixed offset (the Callgrind toggle/client-request instructions, 23..43 Ir), so summary/N = ir_per_call + offset/N

iii_bounding_ge_branchy.note: The branchy longest path runs every correction, which is exactly what the masked op always runs, so the two static bounds are equal; on inputs where every sf_sub borrows (gen_bw: 6 borrows, dbl_bw: 4 borrows) the measured counts are equal. finv is compiled identically in the two primitive builds (22471 Ir inclusive in both).

notes_and_limitations: The task text lists sf_add and sf_neg among the ops with b.cs branches. In secp_field.h they use csel and contain no branch; only sf_sub and sf_add_br do, and sf_add_br is unused by the kernel.
ir_per_call includes the 5 to 7 Ir of the measuring loop and call (harness_loop_ir); the net values subtract it. Use the net values if the call is inlined at the use site.

The measured maximum is the true worst case of the harness build for every primitive when the static gap is zero; otherwise the static longest path over all control-flow paths is higher only because it allows canon_k_exact comparison-chain depths that no input can reach ((4,4), (4,3), (3,4); see the lattice table). static_cfg_upper_bound_ir_per_call is the upper bound that does not rely on that argument.

Translation-unit effect: GCC compiles finv differently in the harness (22471 Ir) than in the unmodified step.c (22435 Ir) and inlines the rare functions differently (rare_anchor is 550 instructions in the harness and 880 in the unmodified binary). Primitive numbers from the harness are therefore tied to this harness build; for finv-containing primitives they are conservative by about 36 Ir per finv call. The whole-function static bounds of the unmodified binary are given as the independent check. With the leaf wrappers present in the same translation unit finv became 22569 (bounding) and 22573 (branchy) Ir and the bounding-vs-branchy comparison was off by 4 Ir; the leaf wrappers were therefore moved to separate binaries.

f_single variants gen_bw and dbl_bw (every sf_sub borrows) could not be built for some x selectors (16 variants unavailable) because no such input exists for the fixed x; add_single has them (equal in both builds).

The rare_2cycle and rare_anchor forced scenarios (generic path, fast canon_k, no distinguished point, full ring without a hit) are not worst cases; they only measure the cost outside the primitives. The inlined harness copies of those functions differ from the unmodified binary, so the own-line costs are an estimate for the production code.

Instruction counts only (Ir); no memory-system effects are measured. The measurement of a primitive covers one fixed input per call; the bounding build is data independent except for the control branches enumerated above, which are forced.
